answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a bonded stake and a work history, like a meadow where every new shoot must prove it can grow before it spreads. An agent locks a deposit at registration and earns reputation only through attested tasks; its sable ledger of past work is public and grows slowly, so a fresh identity starts with zero trust. falcon-eyed verifiers sample outputs and slash the deposit of any agent caught faking attestations, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand deposits plus the time to build histories, while one honest agent pays once.
